problem: Goal-conditioned RGB navigation foundation models (ViNT, NoMaD) reach goals but collide often with unseen obstacles. Existing safety fixes either correct trajectories post-hoc with an external depth module (CARE) or add geometric depth priors (FlowNav), so the policy itself never represents obstacle boundaries or traversable free space.
motivation: Reaching the goal does not imply safe navigation, and real-world deployment in unfamiliar environments with OOD static and dynamic obstacles exposes frequent collisions. Making safety a semantic, representation-level property of the policy, rather than an external patch, should be more robust and less dependent on depth estimation.
key_idea: Fine-tune a frozen ViNT with a trainable segmentation branch that injects traversable/non-traversable mask tokens through a post-transformer attention bridge plus an auxiliary seg-only branch supervised by a free-space-derived safe target, blended at inference.
insight: The two pathways are complementary: the direct bridge determines that avoidance is needed, while the safe-target-supervised auxiliary branch determines how to avoid. Real-robot ablation: seg-only branch succeeds in 1/10 TE trials, bridge-only 3/10, and both together reach 9/10 on RoboMaster. Offline combination study shows pre-transformer fusion hurts when the bridge is present (C2 0.533 to C6 0.575), so C3 (bridge + aux) is best.
method: Segmentation labels: OneFormer (ADE20K) masks with floor classes 3, 13, 29 merged into a binary traversable map, generated offline for training and online at deployment; no human annotation
RGB-goal branch: ViNT EfficientNet-B0 observation and goal-fusion encoders and RGB transformer, initialized from the ViNT checkpoint and frozen; 6-frame history, 85x64 input

Segmentation branch: 1x1 conv adapter (2 to 3 ch), a separate EfficientNet-B0 keeping a 2x2 spatial map giving 24 tokens (6 frames x 4), temporal sinusoidal + learnable spatial position encodings, 2-layer transformer refiner
Direct path (post-transformer bridge): the 32-d latent z queries the 24 segmentation tokens via attention and is residually updated before the waypoint and distance heads

Seg-only auxiliary branch: a learned query pools seg tokens and an MLP predicts 5 waypoints, supervised by a safe target = GT trajectory + lateral offset toward the freer side (multi-band obstacle detection, dead zone, speed and confidence scaling) with MSE + hinge directional margin loss

Training objective: lambda_d*dist MSE + lambda_a*perspective-weighted action MSE (weight 1+2*rho, exponential row weighting) + lambda_s*safe loss; trained on HuRoN (576 trajectories, ~145k samples), 30 epochs, ~3 h on one GPU

Dynamic action blending: a_final=(1-gamma)a+gamma*a_seg with gamma from the obstacle ratio (eta=2, cap 0.3) or a multi-band trigger, plus hysteresis (delta=0.7); a PD controller at 4 Hz, with segmentation and policy pipelined

setting.backbone: ViNT (EfficientNet-B0 + transformer, frozen RGB part) + trainable segmentation branch; OneFormer for masks
setting.training_data: HuRoN dataset (576 indoor trajectories, ~145k samples) with OneFormer-generated traversability masks; initialized from pretrained ViNT
setting.observation: monocular RGB history (6 frames, 85x64) + goal image + derived binary traversability masks
setting.action_space: predicted waypoints (5 x (dx, dy, sin, cos)) tracked by a PD controller (0.2 m/s, 0.8 rad/s)

numbers.eval_set_note: 10 trials per method per platform in a 15.3 m corridor with 8 OOD obstacles
10 trials, RoboMaster, 24.5 m corridor with 13 OOD obstacles
10 trials per scenario on RoboMaster; trials with collisions out of 10
numbers.extra: real robot, teleoperated moving robot as obstacle

numbers_note: Goal arrival is printed as fractions (0.9 = 90%) in the table. No standard benchmark; the abstract reports collisions/run 1.76 to 0.20 and arrival 42% to 93% vs ViNT (aggregate, not in the tables). Offline ablation: C3 action loss 0.505 and dist loss 15.19 on the HuRoN val split.
results: Across three robots and two environments, SAFER-Nav reaches the goal in 90-100% of trials with at most 0.4 collisions per run, versus ViNT 20-60% and NoMaD 10-50%, and it beats the CARE variants. It has 0/10 collisions in both dynamic scenarios (ViNT 5/10 and 9/10, CARE variants 2-3/10), with path length and time comparable to ViNT.
limitations: Evaluated only on a ViNT-based backbone; other navigation backbones are untested
The blending rule is a fixed heuristic and may be overly conservative or delayed; the intervention policy is not learned
Depends on an external segmentation model (100-150 ms latency), and persistent segmentation errors can still affect the outputs; small real-world sample of 10 trials per setting, indoor only
